groups.directions: In each of the questions below, two statements are given followed by two conclusions. You have to take the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts. Read all the conclusions and then decide which of the given conclusions logically follows from the given statements, disregarding commonly known facts.

questions.text:
Statements:
Some cats are dogs.
All dogs are birds.
Conclusions:
I. Some cats are birds.
II. Some birds are dogs.

options.label: C
options.text: Either conclusion I or II follows

options.label: D
options.text: Both conclusion I and II follow

questions.explanation: Statement 1: 'Some cats are dogs' means there is an intersection between Cats and Dogs.

questions.text:

II. Some pens are erasers.

options.label: C
options.text: Neither conclusion I nor II follows

options.label: D
options.text: Both conclusion I and II follow

questions.explanation: Statement 1: 'All pens are pencils' means the Pens circle is entirely inside the Pencils circle.

groups.directions: In each of the questions below, three statements are given followed by some conclusions. Decide which of the given conclusions logically follows.

questions.text:
Statements:
All rains are clouds.
Some clouds are storms.
No storm is a thunder.
Conclusions:
I. Some rains being storms is a possibility.
II. Some clouds are not thunders.

options.label: C
options.text: Both conclusion I and II follow

options.label: D
options.text: Neither conclusion I nor II follows

questions.explanation: Conclusion I: Rains are inside Clouds. Clouds intersect Storms. There is no direct negative relation between Rains and Storms, so they can intersect. Thus, possibility is True.

questions.text:
Statements:
Some books are pages.
All pages are covers.
Some covers are words.
Conclusions:
I. Some books are covers.
II. Some pages being words is a possibility.

options.label: C
options.text: Both conclusion I and II follow

options.label: D
options.text: Neither conclusion I nor II follows

questions.explanation: Conclusion I: Books intersect Pages, and all Pages are inside Covers. Therefore, the intersection of Books and Pages is also inside Covers. Thus, some books are covers. (True)

questions.text:
Statements:
No blue is red.
All red are green.
Some green are yellow.
Conclusions:
I. Some green are not blue.
II. All blue being green is a possibility.

options.label: C
options.text: Both conclusion I and II follow

options.label: D
options.text: Neither conclusion I nor II follows

questions.explanation: Conclusion I: All Red are Green. This means a part of Green is Red. Since no Red is Blue, that specific part of Green (which is Red) can never be Blue. Thus, some green are not blue. (True)

questions.text:
Statements:
All waters are oceans.
All oceans are rivers.
No river is a lake.
Conclusions:
I. No ocean is a lake.
II. Some rivers are waters.
III. All waters being lakes is a possibility.

options.label: D
options.text: All I, II, and III follow

questions.explanation: Conclusion I: Oceans are entirely inside Rivers. Since no River is a Lake, Oceans cannot touch Lakes. Thus, no ocean is a lake. (True)

questions.text:
Statements:
Some tigers are lions.
No lion is a cheetah.
Some cheetahs are panthers.
Conclusions:
I. Some tigers are not cheetahs.
II. Some panthers are not lions.
III. No tiger is a panther.
questions.explanation: Conclusion I: Tigers intersect Lions, and no Lion is a Cheetah. The part of Tigers that is Lions cannot be Cheetahs. Thus, some tigers are not cheetahs. (True)

groups.directions: In each of the questions below, four statements are given followed by some conclusions. Decide which of the given conclusions logically follows.

questions.text:
Statements:
All stars are moons.
Some moons are planets.
No planet is a sun.
All suns are galaxies.
Conclusions:
I. Some galaxies are not planets.
II. All stars being suns is a possibility.
III. Some moons are not suns.

options.label: D
options.text: All I, II, and III follow

questions.explanation: Conclusion I: Suns are inside Galaxies. Since no Sun is a Planet, the part of Galaxies that is Suns can never be Planets. Thus, some galaxies are not planets. (True)

questions.text:
Statements:
Some metals are irons.
All irons are steels.
No steel is copper.
Some coppers are zincs.
Conclusions:
I. Some metals are not coppers.
II. Some zincs are not steels.
III. All irons being zincs is a possibility.

options.label: D
options.text: All I, II, and III follow

questions.explanation: Conclusion I: Metals intersect Irons, which are entirely inside Steels. So, Metals intersect Steels. Since no Steel is Copper, the part of Metals overlapping with Steels cannot be Coppers. Thus, some metals are not coppers. (True)

questions.text:
Statements:
No apple is an orange.
Some oranges are grapes.
All grapes are melons.
No melon is a banana.
Conclusions:
I. Some grapes are not apples.
II. No orange is a banana.
III. Some melons are not apples.
IV. All bananas being apples is a possibility.

options.label: A
options.text: Only I, III, and IV follow

options.label: C
options.text: Only I, II, and III follow

questions.explanation: Conclusion I: Grapes intersect Oranges. Since no Orange is an Apple, the part of Grapes that is Oranges cannot be Apples. (True)

questions.text:

All squares are circles.
Some circles are rectangles.

Conclusions:
I. Some squares are rectangles.

IV. No rectangle is a cone.

options.label: A
options.text: Only II, III, and IV follow

options.label: B
options.text: Only I, II, and III follow

questions.explanation: Conclusion I: Squares are inside Circles. Circles intersect Rectangles. There is no direct link to prove Squares intersect Rectangles. (False)
